page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, adhering to a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor featuring 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. Cache architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Supported instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, and ADX, whereas AVX-512 extensions and AMX matrix instructions are absent. The configuration does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring persistent block storage for filesystem deployment.

Benchmark testing demonstrates strong single-core computational output, where the instance scores 2688.38 on stress-ng single-core tests, placing in the top quartile. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics are lower, with stress-ng multi-core (5388.66), Geekbench multi-core (3412.0), and PassMark CPU (5910.86) scoring in the lower tiers due to the 4-thread execution limit. Memory subsystem performance is mixed: large-block uncached read and write bandwidth register at 44.77 GB/sec and 35.36 GB/sec respectively, reflecting standard throughput, whereas small-block cached read bandwidth and database operations reflect lower comparative efficiency. Text processing, compression tasks (such as single-threaded gzip at 25.8 GB/sec), and small-model LLM generation (118.15 tokens/sec) achieve average performance tiers.

Given its balanced profile, the n2d-standard-4 offers efficient resource allocation for workloads where parallel thread density and local disk IOPS are not principal requirements. Its performance characteristics align with web server hosting, API microservices, staging environments, build workers, and light application runtimes. Workloads requiring sustained high-throughput multi-core processing or intense local disk caching will face tradeoffs stemming from the underlying core constraints and reliance on remote storage.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, paired with 16 GB of RAM. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with dedicated CPU allocation, it features 32 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware support for AVX, AES, and SHA_NI instructions, while lacking AVX-512 extensions and integrated local storage. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-core performance in stress-ng tests, alongside average results in large-block memory bandwidth, single-threaded compression, and small LLM text generation. However, multi-core throughput in Geekbench, PassMark, and parallel decompression ranks in lower tiers due to its four-thread allocation. With a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the n2d-standard-4 provides balanced resource density suited for microservices, standard web hosting, lightweight continuous integration tasks, and intermediate application runtimes where intensive parallel processing or local NVMe storage is not strictly required.
